reasoning:
This is round 5, same request again, with perfect scores. I'm noting a small discrepancy in the report: the grasp frame height range shifted slightly from 0.01-0.03 to 0.01-0.04, which seems like a minor clarification possibly reflecting something the annotator observed in this round's episodes rather than an error worth flagging.

The insert frame also uses a height near 0.04, so widening the grasp frame's range could risk ambiguity between the two—but since fingers-first-drop is the real disambiguating criterion, the height overlap is secondary. Since all steps scored correctly already, there's no clear evidence a change is needed, so I'll stay consistent with prior rounds and refuse all edits, treating the height note as unsettled but low-priority.

revision.refused: The report asks, for the fifth round running, to delete grasp_end on both sides and to rewrite rules 1, 3 and 4 of the subgoal instruction so that a retry points at the peg end of either class nearest the stored grasp_point. This is the identical request refused in rounds 1 through 4, and this round adds nothing to the grounds: its own argument rests on the two ends of a peg lying about ten pixels apart with other pegs far away, which assumes the pegs still lie where they lay at start of execution; but grasp_end is read only at a decision step that shows nothing held after the demonstration is gone, which is exactly the failed-or-dropped-pick case in which the peg may have been nudged, rotated or displaced by the failed grasp, so the entry nearest the stored coordinate can then be the other end of the same peg or an end of a neighbouring peg. The class the demonstration closed on is a distinct fact from the stored coordinate, no later step recovers it when it is needed, so keeping it does not hold one fact twice and dropping it would break NECESSITY in the only situation rule 3 exists for. Committing the deletion now would undo four earlier refusals. The report's incidental widening of the grasp-frame height from about 0.01-0.03 to about 0.01-0.04 is also left out: every one of the fifty steps across five rounds was annotated and answered as recorded under the current range, the grasp frame is fixed by the fingers first dropping from 100% open rather than by height alone, and 0.04 is the height already used to name the final insertion frames for insert_side, so widening it would blur the one distinction the two fields rely on without any failed step to justify it. The report's remaining suggestions (restating grasp_point's purpose, noting it is carried while a peg is held, naming two fields in the carry-forward sentence) describe the failure pattern or follow from the deletion that is not committed; the current text already says to copy the value unchanged at every later step and to carry all fields forward. Five rounds have scored 10/10 on both subgoal and memory, so no transition or field value is unsettled. Nothing is committed this round.
